<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|50|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XVIII.}}</noinclude>and therfore to the whole land of promis, for that cause called the holy land{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The holy land.}}. ''See. S. Hiero. in Epitap. Paulæ. & ep. 17. & 18. ad Marcellam.''

''11. Elias shal come.''] He distinguisheth here plainly betwene {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Elias.}}Elias in person, who is yet to come before the iudgement: and betwene Elias in name, to wit, Iohn the Baptist, who is come already in the spirit and vertue of Elias. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 1, 17. Mal. 4, 5''.}}So that it is not Iohn Baptist only nor principally of whom Malachie prophecieth (as our Aduersaries say) but Elias also him self in person.

''19. Why could not we.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=True miracles only in the Cath. Church.}}No maruel if the Exorcists of the Catholike Church which haue power to cast out diuels, yet doe it not alwaies when they wil, and many times with much a doe: Wheras the Apostles hauing receiued this power {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 10.''}}* before ouer vncleane spirites, yet here cānot cast thē out. But as for hæretikes, they can neuer doe it, nor any other true miracle, to confirme their false faith.

''20. Faith as mustard seed.''] This is the Catholike faith, by which only al miracles are wrought: yet not of euery one that hath the Catholike faith, but of such as haue a great and forcible faith, and withal the gift of miracles. These are able as here wee see by Christes warrant not only to doe other wonderful miracles here signified by this one, but also this very same, that is, to moue mountaines in deede, as S. Paul {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''1. Cor. 13.''}}also presupposeth, and S. Hierom {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Hiero. in vita S. Hilarionis. Niceph. li. 6. c. 17. Greg. Niss. de vit. Gregorij.''}}affirmeth, and Ecclesiastical histories namely telleth of {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Gregorius Thaumaturgus.}}Gregorius Neocæsariensis, that he moued a mountaine to make roome for the foundation of a Church, called therfore and for other his wonderful miracles, Thaumaturgus. And yet faithlesse Heretikes laugh at al such things aud beleue them not.

''21. Prayer and fasting.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Prayer and Fasting.}}The force of fasting and praying: whereby also we may see that the holy Churche in Exorcismes doeth according to the Scriptures, when shee vseth beside the name of {{sc|Iesvs}}, many prayers and much fasting to driue out Deuils, because these also are here required beside faith.

''26. The Children free.''] Though Christ to auoid scandal, payed tribute, yet indeed he sheweth that both himself ought to be free from such payments (as being the kings sonne, as well by his eternal birth of God the Father, as temporal of Dauid) and also his Apostles, as being of his familie, and in them their successors the whole Clergie, who are called in Scripture the lotte and portion of our Lord. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The priuileges and exemptions of the Clergie.}}Which exemption and priuilege being grounded vpon the very law of nature itself, and therfore practised euen among the Heathen ''(Gen. 42, 27.)'' good Christian Princes haue confirmed and ratified by their lawes, in the honour of Christ, whose ministers they are, and as it were the kings sonnes, as S. Hierom declareth playnly in these wordes, ''We for his honour pay not tributes, and as the Kings sonnes, are free from such payments. Hiero.'' vpon this place.

''27. Me and thee.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Peters preeminence.}}A great mysterie in that he payed not only for himself, but for Peter bearing the Person of the Churche, and in whom as the cheefe, the rest were conteyned. ''Aug. q. ex no. Test. q. 75. to.4.''

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XVIII.}}}}}}

{{c|''To his Disciples he preacheth against ambition the mother of Schisme: 7 foretelling both the author whosoeuer he be, and also his folovvers, of their wo to come. 10 and shewing on the contrary side, hovv precious Christian soules are to their Angels, to the Sonne of man, and to his Father. 15 charging vs therfore to forgiue our brethren, when also we haue iust cause against them, be it neuer so often, and to labour their saluation by al meanes possible.''}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel on Michelmas day Septemb. 29. And vpon his Apparition Maij 8.}}{{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=18|verse=1}}}}T that houre the Disciples came to {{sc|Iesvs}}, saying. {{sup|‖}} Who, thinkest thou, is the greater in the kingdom of heauen?{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 9, 34. Luc. 9, 46.''}} {{verse|chapter=18|verse=2}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} calling vnto him a litle childe, set him in the middes of them, {{verse|chapter=18|verse=3}}† and said, Amen I say to you, vnles you be conuerted, and become as litle children, you shal not enter into the kingdom of heauen. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=4}}† VVhosoeuer therfore shal humble him self as this {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Humility, innocencie, simplicity, cōmended to vs in the state and person of a childe.}}∷ litle childe, he is the greater in the kingdom of heauē. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=5}}† And he that shal receiue one such litle childe in my name, receiueth me. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=6}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 9, 42. Lu. 17, 2.''}}* he that shal scandalize one of these litle<noinclude>{{rh|||ones}}</noinclude>
